en.title: Davos next week: steady snow, about 16 cm up high (forecast 23–29 November 2026)
en.description: Next week's fresh snow in Davos: 4–27 cm on the upper slopes and 2–8 cm at the base (23–29 November 2026), best day, best slopes and how sure the forecast is.
en.lede: The question for anyone heading to Davos next week is simple: how much, and where? Between Monday 23 and Sunday 29 November our forecast puts 16 cm on the upper slopes (4–27 cm), 15 cm around 1900 m and 5 cm at the base, with Thursday 26 November as the snowiest day.

p: This week gives little here: 14 cm at the top from 17 to 20 November and 4 cm at the base. Next week is the bigger of the two for Davos, which is the reverse of the western Alps.

sections.h: How the week of 23–29 November adds up in Davos
p: Read from the top down: 16 cm near 2600 m, 15 cm near 1900 m, 5 cm near 1100 m. The low-to-high spread is 4–27 cm at the top and 2–8 cm at the base.
The snow is not spread evenly. The days that matter at the top are Wednesday 25 (3 cm, up to 4), Thursday 26 (6 cm, up to 12) and Sunday 29 (2 cm, up to 5); the rest of the week is close to dry.
The snowiest day up top is Thursday 26 November, with 6 cm in the middle of our forecast (up to 12 cm). That is a fresh coat on the groomers, nothing more.

Go high: depth is safest on Parsenn and the Weissfluhjoch, and the best skiing should be on the long runs from Weissfluhjoch towards Küblis, Davos' classic powder outing. Treat Klosters and Küblis at the bottom of the long valley runs as the weak point.
The base around 1100 m gets 5 cm against 16 cm at the top. That gap says the snow line sits above the village for much of the week: rain or wet snow down low, real snow only higher up.
Davos has several separate areas; Parsenn is the one that gets the most out of a north-west flow.
Not very. The high case gives 27 cm up top, the low case just 4 cm, so whether Davos gets a real fall depends on a storm track that is still undecided.
Book flexibly if you can: the picture for Davos will be much sharper by the weekend.
At the top, next week, our forecast gives St. Moritz (38 km away) 19 cm, Ischgl (40 km away) 18 cm and Livigno (43 km away) 19 cm, against 16 cm here.
Nothing to separate them on snow alone; the choice comes down to the terrain you want.

advice: Off the groomed runs, new snow means new avalanche risk: the Swiss avalanche bulletin is the reference.
Early season: confirm which lifts are open with Davos itself before you travel.
Pack for wet weather in the village: the 5 cm at the base hides a lot of rain.
